The best way to fight these attacks on voting and elections is by registering as many new voters as we can and getting them to vote in November.
Our program costs $3 per new voter. Join the movement with $30 or more right now to register new voters and more >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=062826_4&amount=30]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Voter registration is a core part of how we fight back against suppression, folks.
How do we do it? We maximize your impact by focusing on the underserved and ignored portions of eligible voters. The unregistered, eligible citizens. Previous voters who let their registration lapse. Anyone who feels disregarded and disconnected from the political process.
Why them? Candidates and their political campaigns target those most likely to turn out. They hyper-focus on "persuadables" and "reliable partisans." Rather than trying to compete with their resources, we maximize your impact by speaking directly to Americans who feel left behind as they lose their fundamental rights.
We drive these eligible citizens to participation by helping them understand the stakes and showing how their vote matters . That's why our voter registration efforts are so important: Everyone should vote and feel invested in the outcome.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=062826_4&amount=30]

New voter registration -- at a cost to us of just about $3 per new voter -- is the whole ballgame. I’m going to be fully transparent: we are $77,283 away from hitting our end-of-quarter fundraising goal. [_**Before I go on, would you consider contributing to our campaign before our deadline?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134210819/630472516/-331877025?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOQ12_260628_T1_3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YTFmZDM3YS00ZDczLWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1C_Yl54dj--PgbviwXomuTPdb3AG0SqE5v4FlN228FY=)

Look, I’m a business guy – I’ve spent my entire career following the money. And I believe that if you're putting your hard-earned dollars into something, you deserve a straight answer about where it goes. So here it is.

**When you chip in to this campaign, your donation goes to work in three places: reaching voters, organizing them, and turning them out.**
* Reaching them requires running TV and digital ads, getting campaign literature printed and in mailboxes, and holding in-person events across the Commonwealth to get our message out there.

* Organizing means people on the ground – paid staff, volunteers, folks out knocking doors.

* And turning them out means a strong Get Out the Vote operation in the fall – mobilizing voters to make their voices heard in one of the most consequential elections I’ve seen during my time in public service.

And I've got to tell you, every one of these investments does double duty right now. Virginia has _several_ competitive House seats on the ballot that could determine control of Congress.

**That means when this campaign builds a strong campaign infrastructure, it’s not just going towards holding this Senate seat – it’s laying the groundwork to elect Democrats across Virginia and flip Congress blue.**

subject: It’s official: We’re up against Steve Hilton
body:
**BREAKING NEWS: I’m officially up against MAGA Republican Steve Hilton in the general election, Peter.**
I urgently need your support to take him and the MAGA money machine on.
[**Will you please split $5 between my campaign for California Governor and Gina Hinojosa in Texas to help keep a Democrat in the governor’s office?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260628_3_becerra.qtIOnD&refcode=em20260628-1450&amount=5&t=1&akid=1450%2E299639%2E-sTyi0)
I have never shied away from the biggest fights. Whether it was suing Trump 122 times as Attorney General or taking on the drug companies as Secretary of Health and Human Services, I have always fought for California families.
And that doesn't change now.
Steve Hilton may be Trump’s handpicked lackey, he may have gotten his endorsement, and he may have millions from the MAGA machine behind him, but I’m not afraid to take him on.
Because in the fight for the future of California, I will not leave any stone unturned. I will do everything in my power to make sure California does not have a leader who acts as a rubber-stamp on Trump’s policies.
But I can’t do it alone. Hilton is going to have millions in resources with him, ready to pummel us into the ground with attacks. We can’t let him succeed. We need to be ready to fight back to keep California out of MAGA hands.
[**Peter, can you please split $5 between my campaign for California governor and Gina Hinojosa to help us take on Steve Hilton and WIN?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260628_3_becerra.qtIOnD&refcode=em20260628-1450&amount=5&t=2&akid=1450%2E299639%2E-sTyi0)

Thank you for standing with me time and time again. Let’s do this!
Xavier

name: Wes Moore
subject: One promise
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1563%2E1086043%2ESwSTsj)
I didn’t come from a political family, Peter.
When I was young, I wasn’t thinking about politics. I never thought I would run for governor.
My father passed away when I was 3. I had handcuffs on my wrists by 11. My mother didn't land a job with benefits until I was 14.
What changed my life wasn't luck. **It was people who believed in me, invested in me, and refused to leave me behind.**
That's why -- as a combat veteran, a father, and now the first Black governor of Maryland -- I've built everything around one promise: a state where every kid, every worker, every family gets that same chance.
But a Maryland that truly leaves no one behind doesn't happen on its own. It only works if we do it together.
Your grassroots partnership is what will turn that promise into action. **Better schools, safer streets, a real shot for the next kid who feels like the system already wrote them off.**
**[That’s how our administration will lead the way forward. If you're able, will you chip in $5 before our end-of-quarter deadline to help us keep leading the way here in Maryland?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260628-2.Z9Kh2-&refcode=em-20260628-2&t=2&akid=1563%2E1086043%2ESwSTsj)**

subject: Why I will not let this one go
body:
This was never about a bad housing bill.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019f10f46d18-92f57fb5-1573-479c-8309-aaa0453ee80f-000000/Z0eUikZjKN8SmmmnZsZXr0wpmdK-Y-lICdkOegRPJxc=452)Patriot–I want to be honest with you about why this fight matters so much to me.This was never about a bad housing bill. It is about whether the people who run our elections will ever be required to do the most basic thing: confirm that the person voting is a citizen, and that the person voting is who they say they are.The SAVE America Act demands exactly that. Proof of citizenship to register. A photo ID at the ballot box. You need an ID to board a plane, open a bank account, or pick up a package at the post office. Casting a vote in an American election should be held to at least the same standard.For too long, the Senate has found a reason to stall. This past week, the President decided the waiting was over. I have rarely seen a clearer moment to back him up.So this evening, I am asking for one thing. Post on social media. Tag the President. Tell him to veto this housing bill, and that you are with him.

Proof of citizenship to register. A photo ID at the ballot box. You need an ID to board a plane, open a bank account, or pick up a package at the post office. Casting a vote in an American election should be held to at least the same standard.For too long, the Senate has found a reason to stall. This past week, the President decided the waiting was over. ->-> Hillary Clinton won the popular vote by nearly 2.9 million.

->->-> But the Electoral College overruled her victory!!

**[We can't let something like that happen again! That's why Sen. Elizabeth Warren is SOUNDING THE ALARM:](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/74972?t=7&akid=24415%2E4449941%2EA8AoM0)**
[](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/74972?t=8&akid=24415%2E4449941%2EA8AoM0)

If every Democrat reading this signs our petition, we will reach our 125,OOO signature goal within minutes and gain traction for this urgent legislation in Congress. [**_Please add your name immediately:_**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/74972?t=9&akid=24415%2E4449941%2EA8AoM0)
[Sign to demand Congress abolish the Electoral College →](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/74972?t=10&akid=24415%2E4449941%2EA8AoM0)

subject: They tried to drive Scott out of the SF Trans March
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott WIENER FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | Peter,

**This weekend,_The New York Times_ reported on something that should concern every one of us.**

Scott Wiener, one of the country's most outspoken champions for transgender rights, was surrounded and chased out of San Francisco's annual Trans March after a group of protesters followed him through the event shouting insults and accusations.

Scott said it was the first Trans March he had missed since attending the very first one in 2004.

Here's what stood out to me: The Times didn't just cover what happened.

They reminded readers _why_ Scott was there in the first place.

For years, Scott has been one of California's strongest advocates for LGBTQ equality. He authored landmark legislation protecting transgender Californians, fought to expand civil rights protections, and has never backed away from defending the LGBTQ community, even when doing so made him a target.

In fact, the article notes that Scott has received threats over his support for transgender rights from the far right, while now facing harassment from activists on the left as well.

That's what leadership looks like. Scott doesn't change his values depending on who's yelling the loudest.

He keeps showing up.

**Now he's running to become the first openly LGBTQ person ever elected to represent San Francisco in Congress. It's a historic opportunity to send one of the nation's most effective champions for equality to Washington.**

Peter,
Currently, there are no vacancies on the Supreme Court. But make no mistake: the knives are already out.
Justice Samuel Alito is 76 years old and expected to retire within weeks. Justices Clarence Thomas and John Roberts will likely follow before Trump's second term ends.
And according to the Washington Post, the auditions for Trump's next SCOTUS picks have already started:
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001V17H5ZzZRkrlRJ49MV-PsBYtXYTu4X0d6X9umVfgsGGBv3vGCkhWlDNZwX7K7WR_Sc8YmZTXlq-htlCFYzc_12-ojkiqkWPsTF6A0xtdJNtziB3KgPkjtdD7HHXgyESClCv6Kn_Bj-qCODB1jPN_jxmh6X_D9nle6aTlA1jVct5PMx78QCJkz6JAmUpwEhIDYP6bPXXVWMLuZwqRo1yUsClAB_4rA59fTVWCIEsw4unMV0ihQVfurw==&c=jz4hvlpJ-X3MVJqsAgzqb9jK-EgnXj4MfIPOT1gmNyd8jRlLFzSjyg==&ch=E2-Y9S-S-rZKmAMRUpA3y0e1XVaCkCNqYjjWt-8fPoZzg8R6WDJGHA==)

Conservative judges across the country are writing increasingly unhinged opinions designed to catch Trump's eye, signaling their loyalty before a seat even opens. One opened a dissent with a crude term for male genitalia. Another reversed his long-held position on birthright citizenship almost overnight.
These judges are competing for a lifetime appointment, and whoever wins will sit on that court for decades. This is the endgame. Trump replaces three older justices on the court with younger extremists, and liberals are locked out of the Supreme Court for an entire generation.
This is how Trump's America becomes permanent.
The only way out of this nightmare is to expand and rebalance the court, and it does not require a constitutional amendment, just a law passed by Congress. That means Democrats must take back the House, Senate, and White House by 2028 and have the courage to act.
That is what our Unpack Our Courts initiative is building. But we cannot wait until 2028 to fight. This November we are protecting state Supreme Courts in Nevada, Kentucky, Montana, Michigan, and Minnesota and backing Democrats in critical races while we build the national movement for federal reform. Every piece of this fight is connected and every race matters.
Over 100,000 Democrats have already joined our fight. We are building the infrastructure to reform the court right now, while there is still time to stop this. But we need more support to match what Trump's dark money machine is deploying:

In a recently unveiled lawsuit the DOJ will now attempt to axe the National Voter Registration Act which prevents states from purging their voter registration rolls in the 90 days prior to an election. | == | If their suit is successful red states would be able to cull their voter files of millions of Democratic voters the day before the election thereby ensuring these voters have no way to update their registration or challenge their erroneous removal from the registration file. In a 2024 shadow docket ruling (the U.S. Supreme Court's emergency non-merits docket, used for expedited immediate relief) they ruled this practice was constitutional though the ruling only applied to a unique scenario in Virginia. But now the Court appears ready to make this the law of the land. When they do this, there will be nothing standing in the way of every Republican Governor in America purging their registered voters list on Monday, November 2nd, the day before the election and removing every registered Democratic voter from their rolls. These voters will show up at the polls ready to vote only to be turned away and told too bad, so sad as it will no longer be possible to reregister. If they challenge their removal, the appeal decision will only come long after the election has passed. And second, ensure that the moment Democrats reclaim control in DC that we take immediate action to eliminate the Supreme Court's conservative majority by any means necessary including by packing the court. Defend our Courts performs both of these functions. ## US and Iran Agree to Halt Strikes
After a weekend of fresh strikes, the United States and Iran have [agreed to stand down and meet Tuesday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOiPnmPincHEbutx2S-Tg4-DEYGQfwubtV-wrbDkaaUbf93Ubby6muD7-uwUthTyueNSERFjGvcbi1tklqlTiCythwjrlbQQOknHJwIzexfQZ-9bbgAgoWrQXpUGBUhfRzjYEI01w3jhurncnvelRaBTK6En73rfRnmtcgrlwrgXv8K68DkoEp_lVgmh6jj5SLt0zx5VmDOmT31i6KS9tsjPRVhvxr4GhgeE4ji7k75Pi7BsYUnwjO3MDw17ZicSo7As7XGEbugkZufSq7LmvyEC3xfrtiCnFKlXT88fiYvr9oj8Jelv4CQAA___54Hvo) in Doha, Qatar, according to a report. Vessels can again move freely through the Strait of Hormuz. The flareup began when an Iranian drone hit an oil tanker near the strait, and American forces answered by [striking missile and radar sites](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFurDAQxvHTmM7IDGDYwsU2vGpfmxIZGMMkxl7Zw6K9fUSUG6T-S6P5fR-P8WHJU1j_2x0NuzgGPLNHZkzjkSnZsFnPmRN9YWb0mOf4HEGBlkpLuI2LJf8em2IxDhGwLtBUXQ8ddF1VF5upprp10GqNVatUNVczgNW61f3S9BNOBZnrmtJwq5Tqa1Xi1C2962pne9VqqEWjcCGOqfyMFHhD59_xhamc4154szE_s6jvAgYBw3me5Z7D1QQMGOSRBQwX6oox-UXAcGR5yeRsU3rLeLAMeMpfpGTMTGGVLtmVPMoZbUZHCQUMNsn7HfQ_B3uRzPI8yXvKuhONWndL_ucn_tOQLwPfAQAA___tq4ih). The Revolutionary Guard then fired drones and missiles at [U.S. bases in Kuwait and Bahrain](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFvgzAQBeBfYzYicyY2DB66sKVrR2TgCNdcbGRfEvHvq1T9B52f9J6-93UZL4GY4vUz3NHLmsaIr8Iognl8FMohboGlSKYbFkHGMqd9BA221raGflwC8TG21eJXREBToW9cBw6ca0y1-fY8G9NP0-xWaxZnrJmmVjtntLV2mvuK_LtNW-gbrTujTzi5pVudWUOnzxaMajUuJCmfvhNF2XDlIz0xn-Z0r9hvIntR5kPBoGCQDTdifmcKhj0xzYeCgaJgjkEoxcAKhnPftqZp6jewziiBKUjKR_0nrW-PVyCpp7DlQFHBUGW_7C9ipmKdavX1Huh3ppJ__fb08BMAAP__RvGC-g), warning that more American strikes would halt talks entirely. Kuwait intercepted two ballistic missiles. Iran also claimed [sole control of the strait](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO4zAMRU8jdwpkyrGdQsU27rLtloZsUbE2smhITIzM6QeaK0xDECTw8N__d5_vNsSQHn_tjoY9zQnPEpEZ8_wqIdu02ciFc3hiYYxYVjpmUNBL1Uu4zc6G-Jm7xhmPCKgbNO0wwgDD0OpmMw7apdWd9asG8Nj2q-366035FtDbdWmCqTTVw61VatTqgsvgRj9ob0d17UGLTqELTPnyn0LiDX380BvzZaW9iWZjPorQfwRMAqb0OahwfQmYKljApOqAUcB0Uo5OVkUBU5WTjl5LxCIdnUlSkislzhQleVk428B12yjvry9pPWOWJ-ITk6v3d6CIaUUBU5ONO84QYyj9IDr12G2IPwn5V7W-DXwHAAD__6Ghjac) for 30 days. President Trump accused Tehran of breaking the ceasefire and warned the regime would "no longer exist" if forced to escalate.
## Colorado Fire Kills 3 Firefighters
Three federal firefighters were killed, and two were hospitalized with burns over the weekend in a sudden [burnover](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0RksMEpKLZx97bd0iJmiGc9MRFMYr2_X3l_4TW3uFc6ujp_vuavSEz743d8YpBc5h2PxiiCdX43qnFfI0uTShs2Qca2lNcMBpw2TsNtTpH4e-67FDIioO0wXP0IHry_2m4Ng0eb8xBvi0vLvV_guriUbr27WxjS4DsKJ804uF2NGa254N2nMXub42gGB1b1BhNJqZe_hXZZMfN3-WC9LOXZcVhFXk3ZXwomBdNxHJdtk885KphOtILJnAGjgsnqTBUzPVbB2vRGzJj0QZzOvun7u-46ctkfeilcakzlLXHVTaKgZtpRwdTVkF4HMVNzXvXm8YzE_-_Ijxx-AvwLAAD__1WXhrE) while fighting wildfires near the Colorado-Utah line. The crew deployed fire shelters as flames overran them on the [Knowles and Gore fires](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFu6zAQRE8jdRSolUzJBYvfuPNvUwprcmltsiYNkpbg2wcKkBOknOI9zMzHdbkiC8f7f3yQrSEtkfYiVCvl5VU4Y1xRaqmZv6hUEiouPRfQYJQ2Cs6LR5b3MrbeBiKgoSXbTzNMME390K4Wewq91mc07ubNyaCetRlp7kkDuhlatodNGzj3Ws-D7ug2-TlMQ8BZnwwMzajJc025-0wc60pB3mmj3Ln0aMWutT5LM_xr4NLAZd_3zifu7mk7EosXjD5wpkJ5Y0cNXG6vHA-B4ujYU6xqP7blqFySlNEndYAHpDKVl9SiAnnKKOrX2GbrnzuLcDFTM-r7A1l-GtU_3bhZ-A4AAP__DNuLog), now merged into the lightning-sparked Snyder Fire, which has burned about 28,000 acres with no containment. Gov. Jared Polis declared a disaster emergency and called in the Colorado National Guard, with [dangerous fire weather](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUD2P3CAU_DV2hwUPL3AFRZrtLm1KCy8P8xJsVvBurf33kaP8g-vmQxrNzK_P5TNQoWP7GXb0nOpy4NkLMmNbvjq1cORQuHOjP9gZC_ZHfS4gwQhpBHwsMVB5L_MYfUIE1CN6ZR1YsFbpMfv5JlVck1JmdlI5tzprAcGEtBqH62Mkf6VJAx9KSqflhKuNLlmdgpM3A3qYJUbi2qbflQ7OmMq7vrBNj7qPxWfmZx_0jwHuA9zP85zeIdd6uQPcrzmXjIEzNvGfhsb0KHjBXr84n9hZnFRiooYihmPDJhrugY4uMm1ZKAO3mwbQU-a9jM3H50mlUDd2mOW2Byr_-vC3Tnx5-BsAAP__TMqHnA) keeping the Southwest primed to burn into the July Fourth week. Meanwhile, in Kentucky, at least four people died as [catastrophic flooding](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQRp_G7rAwOMYpKLZxl223tCZmCLPBYMEkTt7-6v68wW0_fTo6Ov8uywUoUrr9hQ0t-7wkPGpEZizLo1KBFCBy5UJ3rIwR65r3RUk1CjkKdV4cUHwvQ-usR1SoW7S9mZRRxvS6DdbBCk6er15Pxk0a10E753un-tN18gAt2U-aHNW5l3LSssOrcZM32sMkT6PSzSDREefS_c-UOKCP7_zE0q15a6MNzHtt9J9GzY2aj-PofH4dCBy-L42a8cUFNxQ_a6Pmik8sKCrnslWBUFmswFC55D3QKnzM2VG6iTsmfqz3t6DkCBKImh8c2mLdflCMVEfTDPK2AcUvH_5VxKdVHwEAAP__Pq-L-Q) swamped the state, triggering dozens of water rescues and a statewide emergency.
## NASA Races to Save Falling Telescope
NASA is launching a [first-of-its-kind rescue](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ8GOpBZEhsKF9fQ5dor0WKvgy8ORt5NEG9_4l7hr2akkWY035_H_MCY4vb8jW-yEvK80cGJRKjMH44FtxWTsJT4IhZKxC7vMyjQjdINjLPHmM75VnsbiID6mmxnBjBgTNfXq9WdGjq3LHcYde-U6tAPOhgYfaBlAFVHe7UpDWOn1NCrlhbjh2D6gIO6a-irmyIfJZf2b46brBTSmb9UWpffdbKryM5V_6uCqYLpOI7WLXy9uPIKpstegowNHzFIkxem8kXJ5WxeKJhOloZ3dNQUYvehCqa6WL8fMaXI2lQ39XxjTP8X5UeYvhb-BQAA__-AF34u) on Tuesday to save the aging Swift Observatory before it tumbles out of orbit. Liftoff comes aboard the final Pegasus rocket, which an aircraft will release over the Marshall Islands. Intense solar activity has been [dragging the telescope down](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkbGSnDAMhp8GOu0Yw-LdgiIN3aVNyWixvChnbMYSR_btM2wmT3CjRjO_pE_S_-tj-kCOnJ4_caVBQ54SHRJJlcq0CxdMC0YVLfxJohRJ5rxN1tgeTA_2Pnnk-Jq62g-ByFJb09C4m3XWuaatlyGgu147uhp3hre-m-_e4aN5mD50rql5OKeZ3t4bY26tudDD-VtwbcCbufa2rTpDnjWXy-_MSRcK8ZW_qFzmvNZxWFQ3qdoflR0rOx7HcZENZzrVyo7vHOjPFnNB5ZwqO0bc07yQwFucCwat7JhQEFhgwxenJ-ziWwMrx8g5QcgFEBpRyAFYBT45eSgk806wsshZpBl0IcDn2S8HB4X_HyN4UMiFgBUCxigQSl7_LXBCWeHIRRdgrcvgt-PkSu-qzjxX5Pi-Vb9l0Ndg_wYAAP__eXWq_A), and the gamma-ray observatory, in space since 2004, has no engines to climb back on its own. Under a $30 million contract, Arizona startup Katalyst Space built a refrigerator-sized, three-armed robot to chase Swift down and grapple it. If it works, the robot will catch Swift within about a month and raise it to a stable orbit by September. Officials say Hubble could need the same lifeline next. Watch a [video of how it will work here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFq6zAQRb9G3sWMR4pkLbR4jxAKJV0VAt0Y2R7HamXLtSY2-fuS_kK398I5cK6X5uJDDPPtzU_keEjNTHuOxExrc89h9fPoI2dewxdlpki5S0uDgPoA-oC26X2Ij0YVvRuIkGRBrjI1GjSmksXorLctKWk67AhapS1pqOyxArJHi14VwT1poNFWALWEklrT14ORg6_hqFEKBdQHTmv5mcLMIw3xkTZayy5NRXQj85KF_CfwLPC873v5SHe-t_T8n4vnbhTyvAl5en_ptuX1-vGtLgK1nxYh_7OQJ8zF6vplDzGGrI1QcJt8iL8G_lOWzeFPAAAA__-I_nVw).

You can pass a law in America by voting for it yourself, directly, at the ballot box, by a landslide, and watch your state's highest court rule it valid. Then watch it erased within weeks. Not by a recount. Not by a court reversal. By the plain decision of the representatives you elected, who repeal your vote and face no consequence for it at all.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7bdaaea7-9795-4590-950d-30dc31c42852?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This happens in the part of American government almost nobody watches: the statehouse. It is not a glitch; it is the designed output of a machine most people have never had explained to them. And it is not one party doing it to the other, the votes that get erased are often cast in red states, by the very people who send Republicans to the capitol. So here is the question the machine is built to make irrelevant: what, exactly, is your vote worth?
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4ccd442f-fd6f-4841-afe1-1294dcb30f69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The Rigged Map --Part 1: How They Drew the Map](https://substack.com/redirect/4ccd442f-fd6f-4841-afe1-1294dcb30f69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Unrig](https://substack.com/profile/499853335-unrig) and [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| May 12
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4ccd442f-fd6f-4841-afe1-1294dcb30f69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The first two parts of "The Rigged Map" series followed that machine through the maps that decide Congress. This one follows it somewhere more intimate: your state legislative districts, the maps that decide whether your wages rise, whether you can stay home sick, whether you can see a doctor. They are often rigged far more ruthlessly than the lines that decide Washington.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b33ffeb4-9e4a-4e5b-90e6-9aa8aa9b58ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Part 2: How They Closed the Courts](https://substack.com/redirect/b33ffeb4-9e4a-4e5b-90e6-9aa8aa9b58ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Unrig](https://substack.com/profile/499853335-unrig) and [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Jun 10
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b33ffeb4-9e4a-4e5b-90e6-9aa8aa9b58ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Here is how it works.
A gerrymander draws districts so lopsided that one party is all but guaranteed to win them. Once a seat is that safe, the November election stops deciding anything; the only contest that can unseat the incumbent is that party's primary, a low-turnout affair dominated by the most committed voters and the wealthy donors who fund the campaigns.
Win the primary and the general is a formality.
So a representative's real boss is never the broad public; it is the narrow slice that votes in the primary, and the big money behind it. That is all a "safe seat" means, a place where the people who live there have already lost the only election that counts. Build a statehouse out of such seats, and it can defy its own voters and pay nothing for it.
This is why the familiar instincts fail. Voting a straight party line, or studying the issues and voting your conscience, in a safe seat, both happen in November.
November is the formality. The election that chose your representative was the primary, and for most people it was over before they knew it had begun. You can be the most informed voter in your district and still be voting in the wrong election. And when the people lose it, the bill comes due in dollars, and in lives. You don't need a theory to see it, only to watch what one state's legislature did to its own voters.
* * *
### Missouri Said yes. The Legislature Said No.
In November 2024, Missourians did something their legislature had refused to do for years. By ballot initiative, the citizen end-run that lets voters write law directly when their representatives won't, they passed Proposition A. It raised the state minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2026, indexed it to inflation after that, and guaranteed workers paid sick leave.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/96ffdcdc-1805-4a13-919e-d95e0dce58de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.firstalert4.com/2024/11/06/mo-votes-increase-minimum-wage-require-paid-sick-leave/](https://substack.com/redirect/06730cdc-c865-4040-9bf1-36875dc5f942?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It passed with 57.6 percent of the vote, nearly 1.7 million yes votes, almost as many as Donald Trump drew in the same state on the same night, which he carried by eighteen points. Vast numbers of Missourians, in other words, voted for Trump and for the measure both. This was not a partisan wish list. It was a supermajority of Missourians, Republicans plainly among them, telling their government what they wanted.
The business lobby went to court first. A coalition including the Missouri Chamber of Commerce, the Restaurant Association, and the National Federation of Independent Business sued, arguing the measure violated the constitution's single-subject rule. On April 29, 2025, the Missouri Supreme Court upheld Proposition A: the summary was not misleading, there was no irregularity, the voters' law was clean. It stood.
So the legislature simply repealed it. House Bill 567 struck the paid-sick-leave guarantee in full and deleted the inflation indexing, freezing the wage after 2026. The House passed it 97 to 49: the yes votes all Republican, the no votes all Democrats but one, a lone Republican who sided with the voters. The Senate passed it 22 to 11, its leadership invoking a maneuver the chamber rarely uses, the "previous question," to shut down a Democratic filibuster. Governor Mike Kehoe signed the repeal on July 10, 2025.
The timing is the part to sit with. The sick leave took effect May 1 and was extinguished August 28, accrued for a single summer, then taken back. Not by the voters who granted it, but by a legislature overruling them six months after the election, and barely two weeks after the state's highest court had confirmed the law was valid.
Ask who actually wanted it gone, and the gerrymandering story and the corporate-money story turn out to be one story.
The repeal was driven by the business groups that had lost at the ballot box, who called the mandate a job killer; the Senate minority leader charged on the floor that the supermajority had acted at the direction of "corporate overlords." That last is a partisan's accusation, not a finding of fact, but the structure underneath it is not in dispute.
A legislature drawn to be safe does not have to fear a statewide majority; its members answer to the primary, and the primary answers to money. Fifty-eight percent of Missouri can vote yes and it changes nothing, because the maps mean the people who voted yes were never the people their representatives feared.
* * *
### The Override Beneath the Override
It is worth asking why those maps look the way they do, because Missouri's voters tried to fix that too, and were overruled there first.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a4e9d825-37ae-4cce-b1a4-edc3915be032?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.komu.com/news/state/missouri-supreme-court-upholds-proposition-a/article_90b24797-8d98-42aa-8c57-221e147eda6f.html](https://substack.com/redirect/a8934ce7-e745-4691-9309-d8c013289eca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Previously in 2018, the same electorate passed Proposition A. It won with 62 percent of the vote, carrying 80 of the state's 114 counties. It handed legislative mapmaking to a nonpartisan demographer and required districts drawn for fairness and competitiveness, an attempt to outlaw the gerrymander and force the legislature into seats it could actually lose. An Associated Press analysis found the formula likely would have let Democrats cut into the Republican supermajority as soon as 2022. To the people holding those safe seats, it was an existential threat, and they treated it as one.
So before the new system drew a single map, the legislature moved to kill it. It put Amendment 3 on the 2020 ballot to repeal the reform voters had just enacted, demoting fairness and competitiveness to the bottom of the criteria. The way it was sold is the part a court ruled on: the ballot summary led with a token tightening of lobbyist gift limits while barely disclosing that it gutted the redistricting reform underneath.
A judge called that summary "misleading, unfair and insufficient," and wrote that the legislature "seeks to override the recent, clearly expressed will of Missouri voters." Bankrolled almost entirely by the Missouri Republican State Committee, it passed with 51 percent, and many voters, a Brennan Center analyst noted, likely did not understand they were repealing what they had passed two years before.
It was not a clean repeal, Amendment 3 kept the popular ethics reforms, and there is a fair argument that engineering competitiveness carries distortions of its own. But the heart of it is not in dispute. The voters tried to make their legislature reachable. The legislature reached back and took the tool away before it could be used.
* * *
### Utah: even the failure failed by accident
It is tempting to think the system has a backstop, that somewhere, a check kicks in. Utah is the cautionary version of that hope.
In November 2018, Utah voters passed Proposition 3, a full Medicaid expansion covering an estimated 150,000 people, with 53 percent of the vote. Weeks into the next legislative session, the Republican supermajority passed SB96, replacing it with a narrower plan that covered roughly 48,000 fewer people and added a work requirement. Governor Gary Herbert signed it before the voter-approved version ever took effect.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ab8cc4fb-1883-41b6-a77e-d89385ce7760?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.facebook.com/prop3utah/](https://substack.com/redirect/6fdd51a9-9715-4b51-9e04-518ceb36258a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It should have stuck, except the legislature had tried to have it both ways, covering fewer people while still drawing the enhanced federal funding the Affordable Care Act reserves for full expansion.
Washington refused; a fallback buried in SB96 then triggered full expansion anyway in 2020, and the voters got, eventually, what they had voted for. But the rule that saved them was written to discipline cost-cutting states, not to protect ballot initiatives, and even then it was close, the federal administration overruled its own Medicaid agency, which had been ready to let the override stand. The maps let Utah's legislature defy 53 percent of the state freely. What defied the legislature back was a financing technicality the voters had no hand in. Even the failure failed by accident.
* * *
### The Bill In Lives
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b00ae204-ae1b-4e9f-88c4-d7156da24ce1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://friendsofmountmoriahcemetery.org/about/notable-burials/native-american-sailors/](https://substack.com/redirect/be762d04-a2f7-469b-af08-df318391a56e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Missouri ledger is measured in dollars: a frozen wage, sick days revoked. The Medicaid ledger is measured in lives, and the arithmetic is grim. Researchers studying the states that refused expansion estimated that roughly 15,600 people died who would have lived had those states expanded Medicaid as the law intended, deaths concentrated among older, low-income adults, from precisely the conditions that medical care prevents.
That is the cost of the divergence, and the ballot initiative is what proves it is a divergence, not a preference. In seven Republican-led states, Maine, Idaho, Nebraska, Utah, Oklahoma, Missouri, and South Dakota, voters used the initiative to expand Medicaid over legislatures that had refused for years.
When an electorate votes directly for coverage while sending representatives who block it to the statehouse, you can no longer say the legislature reflects the will of its constituents. The constituents are on record, in the same election, wanting the opposite. That gap is not a matter of interpretation. It is the rigged map, rendered in mortality tables.
* * *
### What 90 percent can't buy
Almost nothing pulls nine in ten Americans to the same side. Universal background checks for gun buyers do, support runs near ninety percent, across nearly every line that supposedly divides the country. And it changes nothing. In a system that answered to the public, that near-unanimity would be law; in a system of safe seats, it isn't. The ninety percent lives in the general electorate, and safe-seat legislators don't answer to the general electorate. They answer to the primary, where that consensus thins out, so they can defy nine in ten Americans and never pay for it.
* * *
### The only safe place left
Step back and it reads as a single argument. Missouri's voters raised their own wages and were overruled; they tried to fix the maps that made the overruling possible, and were overruled there too. Across the country, voters bought themselves health coverage their legislatures had denied, and watched those legislatures move to shrink it. This is not one party against another. The measures pass in red states, carried by Republican voters; the overrides answer less to ideology than to the wealthy donors the safe-seat primary rewards. It is the moneyed few against an electorate that keeps voting the other way and keeps getting reversed.
Missouri's organizers drew the obvious conclusion. They have filed a new constitutional amendment for the November 2026 ballot, this time to write the minimum wage and paid sick leave directly into the state constitution, where the legislature cannot reach them.
Their organizing director put the stakes in a sentence: **" No right is safe if it is not in your constitution."** It is a remarkable thing to have to say about laws the people already passed, that the only way to make a vote count is to put it where the legislature is forbidden to touch it. The people can win, and win decisively, and still have to wonder whether it will be allowed to stand.
If there is a way out of this, it does not begin in November. It begins in the primary, the election that actually decides who represents you, and the one almost engineered to be ignored.
The information you would need is not secret: when your primary is, who is running, what they have done with their power, and who pays for their campaigns. It is simply scattered, a state office here, a disclosure database there, a record filed somewhere most people never think to look, kept far enough apart that almost no one ever assembles the whole picture.
That is not an accident either. A public that cannot easily see who represents it, or who funds them, is a public that is easier to overrule. Gathering those scattered pieces into one place, where any voter could find them before the election that actually counts, is the work all of this makes necessary, and the work this project means to take up next.

What the rigged maps cost, how Missouri's voters tried to fight back, and were overruled twice by the statehouse they elected. | | and | Jun 29 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | You can pass a law in America by voting for it yourself, directly, at the ballot box, by a landslide, and watch your state's highest court rule it valid. Then watch it erased within weeks. Not by a recount. Not by a court reversal. By the plain decision of the representatives you elected, who repeal your vote and face no consequence for it at all. | | ---|---|--- This happens in the part of American government almost nobody watches: the statehouse. It is not a glitch; it is the designed output of a machine most people have never had explained to them. And it is not one party doing it to the other, the votes that get erased are often cast in red states, by the very people who send Republicans to the capitol. So here is the question the machine is built to make irrelevant: what, exactly, is your vote worth? | | | | | and | | ---|---|--- | May 12 | The first two parts of "The Rigged Map" series followed that machine through the maps that decide Congress. This one follows it somewhere more intimate: your state legislative districts, the maps that decide whether your wages rise, whether you can stay home sick, whether you can see a doctor. They are often rigged far more ruthlessly than the lines that decide Washington. | | | | | and | | ---|---|--- | Jun 10 | Here is how it works. A gerrymander draws districts so lopsided that one party is all but guaranteed to win them. Once a seat is that safe, the November election stops deciding anything; the only contest that can unseat the incumbent is that party's primary, a low-turnout affair dominated by the most committed voters and the wealthy donors who fund the campaigns. Win the primary and the general is a formality. So a representative's real boss is never the broad public; it is the narrow slice that votes in the primary, and the big money behind it. That is all a "safe seat" means, a place where the people who live there have already lost the only election that counts. Build a statehouse out of such seats, and it can defy its own voters and pay nothing for it. This is why the familiar instincts fail. Voting a straight party line, or studying the issues and voting your conscience, in a safe seat, both happen in November. November is the formality. The election that chose your representative was the primary, and for most people it was over before they knew it had begun. You can be the most informed voter in your district and still be voting in the wrong election. And when the people lose it, the bill comes due in dollars, and in lives. You don't need a theory to see it, only to watch what one state's legislature did to its own voters. Missouri Said yes. The Legislature Said No. In November 2024, Missourians did something their legislature had refused to do for years. By ballot initiative, the citizen end-run that lets voters write law directly when their representatives won't, they passed Proposition A. Vast numbers of Missourians, in other words, voted for Trump and for the measure both. This was not a partisan wish list. It was a supermajority of Missourians, Republicans plainly among them, telling their government what they wanted. The business lobby went to court first. A coalition including the Missouri Chamber of Commerce, the Restaurant Association, and the National Federation of Independent Business sued, arguing the measure violated the constitution's single-subject rule. On April 29, 2025, the Missouri Supreme Court upheld Proposition A: the summary was not misleading, there was no irregularity, the voters' law was clean. It stood. So the legislature simply repealed it. House Bill 567 struck the paid-sick-leave guarantee in full and deleted the inflation indexing, freezing the wage after 2026. The House passed it 97 to 49: the yes votes all Republican, the no votes all Democrats but one, a lone Republican who sided with the voters. The Senate passed it 22 to 11, its leadership invoking a maneuver the chamber rarely uses, the "previous question," to shut down a Democratic filibuster. Governor Mike Kehoe signed the repeal on July 10, 2025. The timing is the part to sit with. | [ ](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)

Dear Friend,
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)Let me tell you about Brenda Brown. For months, she worked the sidewalks of Skid Row in Los Angeles, paying homeless men and women two or three dollars apiece to put their names on voter registration forms — names that could become real ballots, mailed to an address where those people never lived. She was certain no one would ever notice. Who pays attention to Skid Row? Who would ever stand up for a homeless man being used as a tool for fraud? We did. I put on dirty clothes, sat down on that sidewalk, and let her try to recruit me — **with a hidden camera rolling the whole time.** [****](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)**[CHIP IN NOW TO FUND THE NEXT INVESTIGATION →](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)** A few weeks later, the Department of Justice federally charged Brenda Brown. One felony count. Up to five years in federal prison. She has since agreed to plead guilty. And at the press conference announcing the charge, the DOJ did something they almost never do for an independent journalist: they thanked us by name. **They said our footage is what made the case.** Stop and think about what that means. A camera you helped pay for put a real criminal on the path to a federal conviction. Not an op-ed. Not a hashtag. Not a "raising awareness" campaign. A conviction. Consequences. The rarest thing in American life today — a corrupt scheme actually facing justice. **[That is what your support does. It doesn't buy outrage. It buys outcomes.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)** And here is why it reaches your own life, even if you've never set foot in Los Angeles: every fraudulent registration is a real ballot that can cancel out a real vote — maybe yours. When we caught Brenda Brown, we weren't just stopping one woman. We were defending the one thing that makes you a citizen instead of a subject: **the integrity of your vote.** [****](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)**[DONATE NOW AND HELP US CATCH THE NEXT ONE →](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)** It wasn't free, and it wasn't safe. On Skid Row my team was surrounded. **One of my guys was punched in the face and neck**. We were pepper-sprayed. We got out, kept the footage, and published it anyway. I'll be honest with you: almost no outlet on earth would send a reporter to sit on that sidewalk. It's uncomfortable. It's dangerous. There's no advertiser who wants their logo next to it. So it simply doesn't get covered — and the Brenda Browns of the world keep working in the dark. Unless someone shows up. **We show up because you make it possible.** There are more of these schemes, in more cities, operating right now. **[The only question is whether we can afford to be there with a camera when they happen.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)** **[Will you stand with us today?](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)**
In Truth,James O'KeefeFounder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. ****The DOJ thanked us by name. A judge will hand down the sentence. But it started with supporters deciding this work was worth funding — and a camera on a Skid Row sidewalk. The next investigation is already underway.[**Help me get it on tape.**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkb2unTAQhJ_GdBz5h2OgcBEJ0d20KdGyXjjW9Z9sk7x-xIlumeKWO_vNSKP59bF9gPMunj8hkCnt2ErdXE6VLFR4pUCeag0QXaNoN8ml7rnu5XxzorPGogWBHRkxTnJUfBqm7mWm2cJOQGgPFMcM0wiTRJz1Pj33nVPnzB3FtZyF4Hx4Pp4SpJjnA_SIg0ZiAwdPpT0K5Wv3DiE2qJ9HKkgPTKHz5tVarkz9YHJlcq2EV6EHRLKp3QSTa_okOiiQdXCWdOVbCmfvQgZsPRe9i9ZhCxRbH_Y-pwxMrVcLW01XQWJq-R_PpL65O_sKTC1v7z8NIWRwZ2Rq-Sr59Umx3V61lHYwqSGk632qZ1eMzX-c967qkQ38DOD8u2j7_iy_jfwbAAD__2k0n2A)

So it simply doesn't get covered — and the Brenda Browns of the world keep working in the dark. Unless someone shows up. We show up because you make it possible. There are more of these schemes, in more cities, operating right now. In Truth,James O'KeefeFounder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. ****The DOJ thanked us by name. A judge will hand down the sentence. But it started with supporters deciding this work was worth funding — and a camera on a Skid Row sidewalk. The next investigation is already underway. ## Court Halts Harris County Immigrant Fund
The Texas Supreme Court on Friday [ordered Harris County to stop spending](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u6yAQBeDV4A5rGOO_guI17vLaW1oYJjYKBgtInOz-ytnCbaaYI306Oj-3-aadd2H9r3dS5X2Pc6AzeyqF0qzX1VHWwfoY1i2mkONxxEzLjIAdh47jOFvt_GeWlVUL2FFUpEQ_YN8IgL7a1DK0Q9Oa3jQtCKS2HVrRoYSWUNjBQOXUhUGHoxDQoKxFZ0AKXEBSg3I0TAJZV2Kqy0aF3jrf_Se-KNUm7pVXWylHZs0_hhPD6TzP-rGU9xUynC6b4QTXwZ7h9AV4fh6JduImPlPhi4_mkfmmU3L5-oXy4W7f3Zp0KNzTqj3PlF7OUOb3Z7AMpyope5zOe5e7nklYd-38t1L525Avhb8BAAD__2b5hz0) on a $1.3 million fund that pays for immigrants' legal defense in deportation cases. The [justices cited](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb9GOww8GZGCYhu72XZLg_JUEuQZwHHm7zfuL2x_c-895-c5Pq0PPq7fdkdT3guNEa8csBRMo11Xj9lGFyiuG6WY6Tgo4zQCh47xjoEenfXhM8ramYk7LWo0QvWgWsG5qjcjrFzU1Ldidn2r5aR6mLnS0vb40OqBtTd3Ge9AC8FbkI3oZi4FTFxiC1LPleTofKHUlA0Lvm1ewodemJqZ9jqYrZQjV-1XBUMFw3VdzUJv6DY6c6F4hyoYbqoKhs2m5DOb6Yzlw_y--zXZ4imy5Ywus8OeGR27H9XJuOPyIfjcqUrydbc-_E2W_4l6GfgNAAD___ygfeo) "serious doubt" about whether the county has the authority to run the program and noted that once the money is spent, it can't be recovered. Their order is not a final ruling. Attorney General Ken Paxton, who [sued the county](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAQhU9jMiO78JghcLAJ2Wy6ISpwNVhrbGQXQ_ftV7S0J5ikktL73s-fr-kLQwxp_Y07OX4-8pToqpGYqUy4roEqJh9zWrdcUs3HkSvNEyiwUlkJw-QxxNdkGu9m5QfdkNP9J_SdVqpvNocfoL1ZOrQagD6t6Y2dB4UG1azt4pvgbpiyMGitOjCttosyGmZlqAMzLMIo8oFzaXkjpifWR3zlbyrtkvcmuo35qKL7JWAUMF7X1f6tyPdTwHi3ETC-ZQJGUPAhYNT6_znwyTnJelKVG5YSqlzymfglbwcZacUo63kcubB85CLP5PNy7pSYvAz7HtaCiW92U5w_rhBjqLYXRq07hvjOyD9b9tvBvwAAAP__XKOODQ), called it "a major win for protecting taxpayer dollars," arguing the fund unlawfully hands public money to private groups. Harris County, which created the fund in 2020, intends to keep defending it as a due-process measure. Three justices dissented from the pause.
## Aggies, Longhorns Oppose College Sports Bill
Texas A&M and the University of Texas, longtime rivals, [sent a joint statement](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO8yAUhE-DOyx4dnBcUPyNu_ztlhaGZ8wKgwVv42RPv0r2CNuNNJrRfPNxm28mxJD8f7Ojpsea54RnjUiEZTbeB6wmuZiT33JJNR9HrrjMIEBxoTiMszMhPue-cXoRbpQNajlcYeikEEOzadEpGFcczCpRXS0KZYb1cjHDCmvnxqUJ-lUmFIxSig76VioregmL6LGDfrSsF-gC5dLShoQPU9f4zHcsrc17E_VGdFTW_WMwMZjO82xz6l4eg-kFw2B6p7jZ-a8oGNFU5J85JOKVDOGOiThlTui4LV_f_E0akudHyYSWuM0xokdej1yocmOJwdQU7Y4zxBiqGlgv_G5CfO-iv7151_ATAAD__z-NjL8) to Republican Sen. Ted Cruz on Friday opposing his Protect College Sports Act as currently written. The schools wrote that they appreciate Congress' effort but see "key issues with the bill as currently drafted." They said they can't support it in its present form but want to work with lawmakers and the SEC on changes. Cruz, who chairs the Senate Commerce Committee, [wrote the bipartisan bill](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGOpDAQRL_GZEa28cAQEFxCtpdeiBrTA5Ya23L3DrP79ac53R9sVFKpVNLT-_OxfECkmPbfcOIkr0deEl5MKIJ1gX2PyJA2ymk_ck2cS8mM6-KM67XptRuXDSJ9Lb7ZptVso21wssPdDZ01ZmiO6eb9Dbdg74-bN4P169jf0IX7OHZgwZomTu8z07vRWtM539o-GG_dajx2zo9BeYNblFxbOVDwBfygr_zE2oZ8NjQdIoVV90u5Wbn5uq53f2IN2DImEGz3_FRuLhWZlZs3PJWbKxICo3JzgCQXEulQP781h-OMIjrknFj_X-k1FqgSGZJeI5GWrFlgjRS_UYdMhDtqLrkK61KzYBANchAKsoa0aXyVd1R8YvpEzQfUmHbl5qZOW7kiUeR-UN7sJ0T6RyY_8_Gc3N8AAAD__x7TpQ4) with Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., to set national rules on athlete pay, a five-year eligibility limit, and one-time transfers. Cruz has called it the only way to bring order to college sports. The bill [cleared the Senate Commerce Committee](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZEZ2Y-AIHFxCNpdeiPzTA5aMjejWMPP2q5nVPsHmX5Wqvv-35eZSTmX953a0_LzXpeBFGZnxXNy6JiRXYq5l3epZqB5HJfQLKBikGiRMS3QpvxbTROtVnHSDVo9_YOy0UmOzWd-brjOm9x0aPcReBR97r8APyhvjxybZd5kaYNJadWBaPQRlNHhlsAMzBWEUxsT1bHlDxqeje37VB55tqHuT7cZ8kOj-CpgFzNd1tcETHfVkehMC5lBzxhXlvVb2LmcB8_ulgPk4K2Ng-UN8x6QLLA9HhCQJi2OUoe57YkaUPq2SsUjCID86EqdaBMzNaeNxpZwTDaMwat1dyp-N_DuzDwtfAQAA__-GKZDm) on June 18 and now awaits a full floor vote. The Southeastern Conference, home to both Texas schools, opposes the bill as written, as does [the Big Ten Conference](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykzztuxCAQANDT4G6tYSB4XVCkcbdpU1pjM2AkFixA-7l9lFwhF3jS-76tN4op5vBFd7b95cua-dkS9851pRAiN8oulRyOUnMr51kabysCmguYC86ro5jeqx6c3cDNcmArpytOSgJMw2F3mr2nD7NNV6M8AIHSnom0xkle3TxE-4uBwVlKUKhHaXbQEjfQrFDPu9DALvZSx35w5xc1n97lwXXcy31I9uj9bEJ9ClwELlsMnfNYahC4UO1xTyxwMSBBCVyGat35jCnFZiahIdwppj-o_6__sPgTAAD__yRNbTQ).

name: Julia Wolf
subject: Volunteering for Jason Knapp for Congress
body:
Hi Peter,

Thank you again for reaching out and expressing interest in volunteering
with Jason Knapp’s campaign! We are thrilled to have you on board.

This is a pivotal time in our country, and we would love your support.

So we can move forward with our volunteer program, could you please take a
minute to reply to this email with a few quick details?

-

Where are you based? (City, town, or neighborhood)
-

What are your preferred volunteer activities? Let us know which of these
sound best to you (feel free to choose more than one!):
-

Phone Banking: Making calls from home or our campaign office to
connect with community members.
-

Door Knocking (Canvassing): Talking directly with voters in key
neighborhoods.
-

Postcard Writing: Handwriting short, personalized messages on
postcards to targeted voters.
-

Event Support: Helping us set up, manage, and tear down campaign
events and rallies.
-

What is your general availability? (e.g., weekday evenings, weekend
mornings, specific days of the week)

Please don't worry if you haven't done something like this before! We make
sure that all of our volunteers are fully prepared. Before you start, we
will provide you with thorough training, up-to-date campaign literature,
and all the materials you need to feel confident and successful. And more
importantly, we’ll make sure we have fun doing it.

We look forward to working alongside you! Let us know your details, and
we’ll follow up with our upcoming schedule and next steps.

Best regards,
Julia Wolf
Campaign Intern

Find out more:* jasonknappforcongress.com
<https://jasonknappforcongress.com/>*
Support the Mission: *Donate Now
<https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jkforcongress>*

Hey Peter! This is Larry David. Surprised to hear from me? Well, I’m as surprised as you are. You think I wanted to do this? This is cutting into nap time. But I couldn’t say no to Alex Vindman. He’s running for Senate in Florida. I like that Vindman. The man is everything I’m not, which should give you some idea of what a tremendous person he is.
The guy’s a hero — a real one. He sacrificed his career to testify in front of Congress about how Trump tried to blackmail Zelensky, the President of Ukraine.
You know, I’m a nice guy. I don’t like to criticize people, but I’m willing to bet that the woman running against him wouldn’t sacrifice her career for anything. I’m also willing to bet that every vote she’ll ever cast will be because Trump wanted her to vote that way:
“Yes, Mr. President! Whatever you say, Mr. President. You’re the greatest, Mr. President. Build more monuments to yourself, Mr. President? I’ll vote for it! Gut the Affordable Care Act? I’ll vote for it! Go to war with Iran without a plan to end it? I’ll support it. Use your office to enrich yourself and your family? I won’t say a word. Do anything I can to help you distract from the Epstein files? Sure, here's some more UFO footage! Lie every second of every day? I’ll go along with it, because I’m a puppet and I don’t have a mind of my own. I’m just a little sock.”
Vindman is not a puppet. He has a moral compass that doesn’t allow him to sell out. His family immigrated from Ukraine. They had nothing. He loves this country. He loves it so much it’s almost off-putting. I love it too, but come on. Get a life, Vindman! There’s more to life than serving America.
**Now here’s the awful part...Right, you got it. Money. Alas, you can’t get elected without money for a campaign.** I get it if you don’t want to give anything. Who wants to give money to someone you don’t know? Who wants to give money to someone you know?!
[**But even if it’s a small amount, it might be worth it if you elect someone who’s different, who has a backbone, and who’s actually a good guy. And who knows — you might personally need something from your senator one day. And this I guarantee — he will respond. And if he can help you, he will. Last week a $500 million non-profit funded by Anthropic, OpenAI, Amazon and many others was announced. It's called RAISE US and works primarily with state governments to help workers transition to different jobs in the AI age.
I'm glad people are starting to act. But I will say that this kind of effort is an enormous acknowledgment that tons of workers are going to lose their jobs to AI.
Among those already affected by the arrival are those in Silicon Valley. Amidst significant layoffs, folks are witnessing the impact of AI firsthand.
"I was working seven days a week on AI until recently," recalls Clara Shih, the founder of the [New Work Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/7da01f21-201f-4d11-a0c3-3f9104f8997f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "I was running the deployment of AI within Meta to businesses that were using our platform. We rolled out AI agents to serve the needs of over a million businesses, which I was very proud of. The agents managed ad spend, customer service and other functions. But I started to notice something. The businesses told me that the agents worked so well that they didn't need the staffer who had been doing that sort of work."
That hit Clara hard. "I realized that, if we were replacing workers at hundreds of thousands of businesses, AI was going to do the same throughout the economy. When I first heard you talk years ago, Andrew, about the eventual impact of AI on jobs, I thought you were crazy. Now I feel like you were right."
Clara has done just about everything in tech, including starting a successful company after graduating from Stanford with two degrees in Computer Science and stints at Google and Salesforce. Today, she points out data showing AI's negative effect on two popular categories of work for recent college graduates: software development and customer service. "Young people are already seeing fewer opportunities in both of those fields because new tools can do that work more efficiently. And this is going to speed up as AI gets deployed to more functions and companies."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be9f6313-0ace-4b26-a6cb-a65067663396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dd9eea3a-3a1f-47f0-a7ff-af6da27864bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Silicon Valley, "There's a feeling that the gates are closing and that you have to do all you can to get through them right now," Clara relates. But Clara is doing more than just talking about it. She left Meta a few months ago to start the [New Work Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/7da01f21-201f-4d11-a0c3-3f9104f8997f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which launched in April.
"I started hearing from young people who were sending hundreds of resumes out and not getting hired; it started to wear on their confidence and self-esteem. I co-founded the [New Work Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/7da01f21-201f-4d11-a0c3-3f9104f8997f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to help young workers. They pick a field like Marketing, Accounting or Software Engineering at [dearcc.org](https://substack.com/redirect/52cabc03-d8ad-4ec6-b429-a0cceae474e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We put them in pods with others who are similar in background so they have a peer group. We then provide them both human and AI mentoring and equip them with AI tools that would make them valuable to employers."
Clara is new to this but not new to scaling products. "I'm treating this like it's a startup with a purpose of helping people and workers. Everyone's volunteering. One of my co-founders is 25 years old, which is helpful in communicating to young people where they are." Clara is volunteering and the Foundation is a non-profit. I am a big admirer of her spirit; Clara is a rare leader who stepped away from the commercial rewards of AI to address human needs. I have the feeling more and more folks are going to need her help in the days ahead.
For my interview of Clara on the [New Work Foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/7da01f21-201f-4d11-a0c3-3f9104f8997f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/e75cf5af-81e5-4673-b760-8cbb2444fa71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But I will say that this kind of effort is an enormous acknowledgment that tons of workers are going to lose their jobs to AI. Among those already affected by the arrival are those in Silicon Valley. Amidst significant layoffs, folks are witnessing the impact of AI firsthand. "I was working seven days a week on AI until recently," recalls Clara Shih, the founder of the . "I was running the deployment of AI within Meta to businesses that were using our platform. We rolled out AI agents to serve the needs of over a million businesses, which I was very proud of. The agents managed ad spend, customer service and other functions. But I started to notice something. The businesses told me that the agents worked so well that they didn't need the staffer who had been doing that sort of work." That hit Clara hard. "I realized that, if we were replacing workers at hundreds of thousands of businesses, AI was going to do the same throughout the economy. When I first heard you talk years ago, Andrew, about the eventual impact of AI on jobs, I thought you were crazy. Now I feel like you were right." Clara has done just about everything in tech, including starting a successful company after graduating from Stanford with two degrees in Computer Science and stints at Google and Salesforce. Today, she points out data showing AI's negative effect on two popular categories of work for recent college graduates: software development and customer service. "Young people are already seeing fewer opportunities in both of those fields because new tools can do that work more efficiently. And this is going to speed up as AI gets deployed to more functions and companies." | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- In Silicon Valley, "There's a feeling that the gates are closing and that you have to do all you can to get through them right now," Clara relates. # DNC Rules and Bylaws Committee Votes to Strengthen Penalties for Violations of Early Window of Presidential Nominating Calendar
---
| | Last week, the [DNC’s Rules and Bylaws Committee (RBC)](https://us.list-manage.com/UbIbrabq4St?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) voted to strengthen penalties for states that hold or candidates who participate in an unsanctioned contest in the early window of the presidential nominating calendar. The RBC is working diligently to establish a calendar that delivers the strongest possible nominee for president. These strengthened rules aim to enforce a fair and orderly nominating process by providing clarity for both states and candidates. Importantly, these changes are being implemented early in the process, prior to a decision on the calendar and before any candidates are in the field, to ensure fairness to all parties.
**Highlights from the changes include:**
* Increasing the delegates lost for states that host an unsanctioned contest from 50% to 100%, including all automatic delegates.
* Requiring campaigns and candidates to denounce any efforts to campaign on their behalf in unsanctioned contests, expanding existing requirements beyond just a ban on direct participation.
* Prohibiting candidate participation in DNC debates, if that candidate or their campaign violates the early window rules.
* Prohibiting candidates who violate the rules from earning delegates in any early window contest.
* [Implementing a $270,000 fine for any state that hosts an unsanctioned contest.](https://us.list-manage.com/xfFKdMcPozs?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
* Setting clear deadlines for states to establish the dates of their contests.
* Preventing backtracking on penalties for states or candidates who violate the rules.

The strengthened penalties were added via amendments to Rule 21 of the 2028 Delegate Selection Rules. The full meeting was livestreamed and can be found on the DNC’s YouTube page [here](https://us.list-manage.com/14orKbUwwjl?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e).
_**RBC Co-Chairs Minyon Moore and James Roosevelt, Jr., released the following statement:**_
“Today, the Rules and Bylaws Committee completed its work on the 2028 Delegate Selection Rules, creating a fair, efficient, and rigorous process to govern how we select our 2028 nominee. These newly-adopted rules strengthen the Delegate Selection Process to ensure maximum participation and clarity.”
_**DNC Chair Ken Martin released the following statement:**_
“Democrats must retake the White House in 2028. Today, the Rules and Bylaws Committee took important steps to bring us closer to that reality by creating a clear and orderly process to deliver the strongest possible nominee.”

_**For too long, many residents of Norwalk have felt that decisions affecting their neighborhoods, schools, businesses, and families are being made without enough input from the people who actually live there.**_
[ Pledge your support](https://substack..UFmXTEcmmXw1Ue6cx4R1mti77q5FfYbi8wf6gWNrXwc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=204031206)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=204031206&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA0MDMxMjA2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODI3MzYxMDYsImV4cCI6MTc4NTMyODEwNiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.dzBxlUSHUYvpe_Eg9r0W3GBVzzeetLpd_Burl9b66SY)
That is why Tricia Ciccone is running to represent Connecticut's 137th Assembly District in Norwalk.
A longtime Norwalk resident, community volunteer, mother, and education professional, Ciccone is building her campaign around a simple idea: government in Hartford should listen to the people of Norwalk--not the other way around.
> **" Norwalk is not just where I live," Ciccone told supporters at her campaign kickoff. "It's my home. It's where I raised my family. It's where I work. It's where I volunteer."**
Having spent years working with children and families through educational and after-school programs while raising her own family in Norwalk, Ciccone says she understands both the strengths of the community and the challenges residents face every day. ([Tricia Ciccone ](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c82765-5b2c-4c4f-b13b-ee310bf72366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Website)
**Putting Norwalk First**
Throughout her campaign kickoff, one message remained constant: Norwalk deserves to have its own voice.
"I want to make sure we're putting our community first," she said. "Norwalk residents need to be heard."
For Ciccone, that means reversing what she sees as a growing disconnect between Hartford and local communities.
"The decisions affecting Norwalk should be guided by its residents--not the other way around," she said. "Hartford shouldn't be telling us what Norwalk needs. The people who live here know our community best."
_That commitment to local control has become one of the defining themes of her campaign._
**Fighting for Affordability**
Like many Connecticut candidates this year, Ciccone says affordability is the issue she hears about most often from voters.
* Families are struggling with rising costs.
* Seniors are worried about remaining in the communities they helped build.
* Taxpayers want greater transparency and confidence that their money is being spent wisely.

> "I know families are feeling the pressure of rising prices," Ciccone said. "I know seniors are looking at affordability. I know taxpayers want transparency and a government that works for them."
Her priorities include lowering energy costs, protecting taxpayers, supporting responsible budgeting, and creating a more affordable Connecticut for working families and retirees. ([Tricia Ciccone ](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c82765-5b2c-4c4f-b13b-ee310bf72366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Website)
**Modernizing Education Funding**
As someone who has spent her professional career working with children and families, education is central to Ciccone's campaign.
_**She believes Connecticut 's current Education Cost Sharing (ECS) formula no longer reflects Norwalk's needs.**_
Rather than relying primarily on property values, she argues that education funding should better account for multilingual learners, special education needs, and the real costs school districts face today.
"Our schools deserve funding based on the needs of our students," she said.
Her campaign calls for modernizing the ECS formula, increasing support for special education, and reducing the pressure local education costs place on property taxpayers. ([Tricia Ciccone ](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c82765-5b2c-4c4f-b13b-ee310bf72366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Website)
**Restoring Local Control**
Ciccone also expressed concern about state policies that reduce local decision-making.
She pointed to recent housing legislation that, in her view, limits municipal authority over planning and development.
Norwalk, she argues, should be able to make decisions that reflect its own infrastructure, neighborhoods, and transportation needs.
"Local communities know what's best for their own future," she said.
**Supporting Public Safety and Small Businesses**
Ciccone says supporting first responders and strengthening public safety must remain priorities.
Police officers, firefighters, EMTs, and emergency personnel should have the resources necessary to protect the community without uncertainty over funding, she said.
She also believes Norwalk's small businesses deserve greater support.
"Our businesses are the backbone of our community," Ciccone said. "We need to support the businesses we already have while creating an environment where new businesses want to invest in Norwalk."
**A Campaign Built on Listening**
Perhaps the most recurring theme throughout Ciccone's remarks was listening.
She promised voters that if elected, she would spend her time in neighborhoods across the district hearing directly from residents.
"My goal is to earn your trust," she said. "To be ethical. To listen. Because I don't think people feel like they're being listened to."
She emphasized that regardless of political affiliation, most residents share the same goals:
* **Affordable living.**
* **Strong public schools.**
* **Safe neighborhoods.**
* **Lower energy costs.**
* **Responsible government.**

Those are the priorities she says will guide her work in Hartford.
**Building a Team for Change**
Ciccone also reminded supporters that campaigns are never about one person.
She encouraged volunteers to knock on doors, make phone calls, and help neighbors participate in the election.
She also highlighted fellow Republican State Senate candidate Justin Perry and Congressional candidate Dr. Michael Goldstein emphasizing that building better representation for Norwalk requires electing strong candidates throughout the entire ballot.
_**" This is a team effort," she told supporters. "None of us can do this alone."**_
Ciccone's message reflects a broader effort among Republican candidates across Fairfield County to work together, support one another, and offer voters alternatives at every level of government.
**A Choice for the 137th District**
Tricia Ciccone believes Norwalk deserves a representative who knows the community because she has lived it.
As a mother, educator, volunteer, and longtime resident, she says she understands both the opportunities and challenges facing local families.
Her campaign is built around practical leadership, fiscal responsibility, local control, improving education funding, reducing energy costs, supporting small businesses, and making government more accountable to the people it serves. ([Tricia Ciccone ](https://substack.com/redirect/b6c82765-5b2c-4c4f-b13b-ee310bf72366?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Website)
This November, voters in the 137th District will have an opportunity to decide what kind of representation they want in Hartford.
To learn more about Tricia Ciccone's campaign, volunteer, donate, or get involved, visit:
**Website:** [www.triciacicconeforstaterep.org](https://substack.com/redirect/66d470f8-32c2-422a-a5f9-4ef26129a377?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Email:** tricia@triciacicconeforstaterep.org
