clean_body: | | | | Boysko Bulletin: We’ve passed a budget that serves Virginians! Dear Peter, Today, the General Assembly met to take action on the Governor’s 14 amendments to the budget that we passed last week. The House and Senate accepted all 14 amendments and the Governor has approved the bill to take effect July 1. Together we have negotiated a fiscally responsible balanced budget that addresses our shared priorities to lower costs for Virginians, invest in our schools and communities, and address the devastating impacts of the federal cuts to healthcare, nutrition and education funding. This budget affords Virginians immediate financial relief including an increase in childcare funding, an increase in the state tax personal deductions, funding to subsidize healthcare exchange premiums on the Virginia exchange, and raises for teachers. The voters asked us to hear the concerns of working families who are struggling and we listened. As passed by the General Assembly, the budget includes the following highlights. Historic Investments in Education $2 billion in new education funding — the largest investment in public education in Virginia history 4 percent raises for teachers and school support staff, and 3.5 percent raises for state employees in each year $577 million for childcare and early childhood education to help working families and strengthen Virginia’s workforce $349.7 million for higher education funding — including $82.5 million to bring down tuition costs, $65 million in new financial aid, and $50 million to support HBCUs Lowers Housing, Energy, Food, and Childcare Costs $60 million in funding for a new mixed-income housing pilot and support for the Housing Trust Fund, $14 million to expand homelessness services, and nearly $12 million in assistance that helps families stay in their homes when financial hardship strikes $25 million in energy efficiency and weatherization programs to help households lower monthly energy costs Directs RGGI credit to residential customers and small businesses to address rising utility costs Protects access to food assistance by providing $135 million to cover federal cuts and $3 million for work supports for people subject to new SNAP and Medicaid work reporting requirements $137.6 million funding increase to expand childcare assistance for families Establishes Virginia’s Paid Family and Medical Leave insurance program to expand access to paid leave for nearly 3.5 million Virginians Data Centers Pay Their Fair Share First-of-its-kind energy consumption tax on data centers to generate $600 million in new revenue annually Protects Virginians from Federal Healthcare Cuts Helps lower ACA health insurance premiums in 2027 for people with low and moderate incomes (138% to 250% of the poverty line) by investing $150 million in ACA Premium Assistance to lower costs for Virginians that purchase coverage through the health insurance marketplace Helps Virginia respond to federal funding uncertainty and changing Medicaid estimates, reduce future state health care costs, and monitor environmental conditions through $969 million in one-time spending, while investing an additional $577 million in general fund money for capital projects Supports access to care by investing $15 million in free clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers to address increased demand Preserves access to care during pregnancy by restoring FAMIS prenatal funding Creates an Adult-Use Retail Cannabis Market Creates a safe, legal, and well-regulated adult-use retail cannabis market that strengthens protections for kids and teenagers, expands safeguards for consumers, and offers greater flexibility for entrepreneurs while prioritizing responsible market development. Cuts Taxes Cuts taxes by increasing the standard deduction by nearly $500 per person to $9,200 for single filers and $18,400 for joint filers; Many of you have written to me with concerns regarding our data centers. I’ve also heard from our environmental advocates that the budget does not go far enough to address the impacts of data centers on our communities. Ensuring that data centers pay their fair share of taxes and do not impact our communities negatively is important. The budget passed by the General Assembly calls for a fee on data centers based on their energy consumption, which is expected to generate a maximum of $600 million each year. It does not include the Senate’s proposal to end the sales tax exemption. This is just the start - the budget also includes a data center study - and I expect additional legislation in the 2027 General Assembly Session. Please join Delegate Sullivan and me for a Town Hall to present commendations and memorial resolutions at the McLean Community Center on June 30 at 6:30 pm. I hope that you are enjoying your summer. Happy Fourth of July! Kindest regards, Jennifer B. Fairfax Public Library: Unearth a Story 2026 Summer Reading Adventure Fairfax County’s Summer Reading Adventure is for youth and adults. Go to and register for the Summer Reading Adventure appropriate for you or your children. Depending on your age, earn ten or fifteen virtual badges by reading or listening to books, reading for 20 or 30 minutes, completing activities or a combination of all three. Once you have met the reading goals for your age/grade, visit your local library branch and receive prizes for finishing the program! Virginia SUN Bucks - Money for Summer Food Virginia SUN Bucks is a one-time benefit to help families with the cost of groceries during the summer when children are not in school. Some families will automatically qualify for SUN Bucks based on participation in SNAP, TANF, income-based Medical Assistance, or free or reduced-price meals at school. Others should apply online, by phone or mail before August 31, 2026. Learn more about SUN Bucks and how to apply . FCPD Connect Fairfax County Senator Boysko toured the Real Time Crime Center recently and learned about the Connect Fairfax County Program. The goal of this Fairfax County Police Department (FCPD) program is to improve public safety by allowing participants to register their security cameras. Property owners can register their security cameras for free with Connect Fairfax County. Once registered, the FCPD will be aware of the camera’s location. In the event of a crime or suspicious activity in your area, FCPD may contact you to see if your camera contains relevant footage. The footage collected could be used to solve crimes, locate missing people, or be used for other law-enforcement investigations. Registering your camera does not grant FCPD access to your footage. After registering your camera, property owners can choose to integrate their security system directly with FCPD. This allows FCPD to access live footage from your camera during emergencies, criminal investigations, or incidents of suspicious activity nearby. Visit this to register and integrate your camera. The referendum on the amendment will take place during the November 3 election and all registered voters can vote for or against the amendment. Team — I have
a story to share with you.

It’s a bit of a long one, so if you’d rather support my campaign with a
[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-june2026.Nocb4p&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_RES_AC_20260629_PM3_V1_S1&t=1002&akid=5054%2E898137%2EPjgXBG ]donation of any amount right now, I’d appreciate it.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-june2026.Nocb4p&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_RES_AC_20260629_PM3_V1_S1&t=1003&akid=5054%2E898137%2EPjgXBG ]DONATE

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-june2026.Nocb4p&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_RES_AC_20260629_PM3_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=5054%2E898137%2EPjgXBG ]Mallory on a podium

One day in October of 2018, I knocked on a door in a winding cul-de-sac in
Troy.

The woman who answered was around my mom’s age. I introduced myself and I
told her that I was running to be her State Senator. I handed her my
literature, and she turned it over a few times.

“Are you married?” she asked.

Yes, I told her. Then I pointed to the picture of my husband, Ray, and our
dog in the literature.

“Do you have any kids?”

No — we had just been married the year before at Eastern Market, right
before I filed to run for office.

“Well, are you going to have kids? And when? And how many?”

She told me that her own daughter was pregnant and that it would be her
first grandchild. Then she stopped me.

“I’m sorry,” she said. “I need to know that my senator is in the office
representing me the whole time. I can’t vote for you. This isn’t a job for
a mom.”

I thought about her own daughter and how she needed an advocate, how she
deserved a voice. Of course, women could do this. Of course, moms should
do this.

But I want to admit something to you — this can get draining.
You see, last summer, during the dreaded gap between the last week of
summer school and the first week of regular school for my daughter’s
pre-school, we messed up.

Somehow, my husband and I timed it completely wrong. In trying to balance
everything, we completely screwed up the dates. We found ourselves
scrambling that week for child care, for someone to be with our brilliant
and endlessly energetic four-year-old, so that we could maintain two
full-time jobs on top of a statewide U.S. Senate campaign.

So many women know that gap.

I found myself worried about telling my campaign team, about stressing
them out, thinking that they wished they worked for any other kind of
candidate. One without a kid. One who doesn’t have to worry about who’s
watching her young child, knowing how hard they worked to arrange a full
schedule of fundraisers, meet and greets, union training facility tours,
and events.

That week, I found myself deeply understanding why so many women just
quit.

Team, we
do this work to write a New American Dream and to ensure that it’s not
just some relic of the past.

We do all of this work knowing that it will mean time away from our
families.

There will be weeks when you find yourself struggling to find childcare,
where you want to tear your hair out. Weeks when you think so much about
how much easier it would be to just quit.

But you don’t. Because we matter. Our voices matter. Because you know that
you can make it easier for the next woman who comes after you. And because
you know that there are so many people who know what you are going through
and who have your back.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/107?c0=mam-em-june2026.wL0jtb&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_RES_AC_20260629_PM3_V1_S1&t=1005&akid=5054%2E898137%2EPjgXBG ]I promise to always have yours. If you’re able, please consider making
a contribution today so we can keep writing a New American Dream together.

clean_body: [ ][IMG] Team — I have a story to share with you. It’s a bit of a long one, so if you’d rather support my campaign with a [ ]donation of any amount right now, I’d appreciate it. [ ]DONATE [ ]Mallory on a podium One day in October of 2018, I knocked on a door in a winding cul-de-sac in Troy. The woman who answered was around my mom’s age. I introduced myself and I told her that I was running to be her State Senator. I handed her my literature, and she turned it over a few times. “Are you married?” she asked. Yes, I told her. Then I pointed to the picture of my husband, Ray, and our dog in the literature. “Do you have any kids?” No — we had just been married the year before at Eastern Market, right before I filed to run for office. “Well, are you going to have kids? And when? And how many?” She told me that her own daughter was pregnant and that it would be her first grandchild. Then she stopped me. “I’m sorry,” she said. “I need to know that my senator is in the office representing me the whole time. I can’t vote for you. This isn’t a job for a mom.” I thought about her own daughter and how she needed an advocate, how she deserved a voice. Of course, women could do this. Of course, moms should do this. But I want to admit something to you — this can get draining. You see, last summer, during the dreaded gap between the last week of summer school and the first week of regular school for my daughter’s pre-school, we messed up. Somehow, my husband and I timed it completely wrong. In trying to balance everything, we completely screwed up the dates. We found ourselves scrambling that week for child care, for someone to be with our brilliant and endlessly energetic four-year-old, so that we could maintain two full-time jobs on top of a statewide U.S. Senate campaign. So many women know that gap. I found myself worried about telling my campaign team, about stressing them out, thinking that they wished they worked for any other kind of candidate. One without a kid. One who doesn’t have to worry about who’s watching her young child, knowing how hard they worked to arrange a full schedule of fundraisers, meet and greets, union training facility tours, and events. That week, I found myself deeply understanding why so many women just quit. Team, we do this work to write a New American Dream and to ensure that it’s not just some relic of the past. We do all of this work knowing that it will mean time away from our families. There will be weeks when you find yourself struggling to find childcare, where you want to tear your hair out. Weeks when you think so much about how much easier it would be to just quit. But you don’t. Because we matter. Our voices matter. Because you know that you can make it easier for the next woman who comes after you. And because you know that there are so many people who know what you are going through and who have your back. [ ]I promise to always have yours. If you’re able, please consider making a contribution today so we can keep writing a New American Dream together. body:
Wisconsin landmarks, Fran style
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260629-2976)
Peter,
AI art versus real art—have you thought about it? Just like the moratorium on AI data centers, _Fran has._
Our volunteers have worked around the clock to contribute to this movement: knocking doors, making calls, donating. They’re even making art! Real, human art, inspired by Fran’s campaign.
Today we’re announcing a limited run of prints we’re calling _Wisconsin Frandmarks_(like landmarks, get it?).
Fran loves Wisconsin and wants to see it thrive. This series is a celebration (and a tiny sampling) of what makes Wisconsin so wonderful, in every corner of the state.
Just 10 prints, 8 works of art, and a midnight deadline to donate before End of Quarter.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=1&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)Frank Hoffman, _Fran for Hayward,_ 2026\. Digital Print.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=2&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)
**_Our opponent, Tom Tiffany, has been very vocal about whether or not candidates in this primary know what a musky looks like. We think this one is pretty accurate — and our musky isn’t AI (if you know, you know)._**
[As you’ve probably heard too many times by now, we’re up against the biggest deadline of the year at the end of June. That’s just 43 days away, and our goal is $100,000 by midnight that night. ](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=3&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=4&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)
Amie Brooks,_Fran for the Milwaukee Public Market,_ 2026\. Digital Print.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=5&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)
Emily Wayland,_Wisconsin for Francesca Hong,_ 2026\. Digital Print.
**We will be giving away one of these limited-edition prints to the first 80 people to donate $200 or more by 11:59pm on June 30th.**
Our volunteers are here, working tirelessly to elect Fran because they believe in her vision. She’s running to protect our workforce from AI: job losses, rights violations. We’re seeing more and more content resorting to AI slop instead of real, human works.
**[If you’re with her, or if you just want to see more real art pushed out into the world—consider contributing $200 or more.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=6&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)**
**[Donate $10 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260629.hRnifV&amount=10&refcode=em20260629-2976&t=9&akid=2976%2E105371%2E8OEEIb)**
With gratitude,
\- Team Hong

subject: Folks... I am worried. Heaven help us if we lose in November.

body:
Please don't skip this 1-minute read. It's Monday June 29, and we have our final, official fundraising deadline coming up in just a few days.

| [ ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/newsom-pan-villegas-wilpert?refcode=em260629&refcode2=2968_4767699_HnKydS&akid=2968%2E4767699%2EHnKydS)
**Folks... I am worried. Heaven help us if we lose in November. We may have enjoyed our last free and fair election. That is why I am asking you to donate to three Democratic House candidates whose elections will determine control of Congress. Do it before tomorrow's FEC deadline ends.**

---|---

Please don't skip this 1-minute read. It's Monday June 29, and we have one of the final official FEC deadlines of the campaign coming to a close tomorrow at midnight.

If you have ever found yourself wishing there was some check on Donald Trump's power, then that means you know the stakes of this election.

So I am asking, humbly, for you to join the 2% of Democrats getting this message who will donate to Richard Pan, Randy Villegas, and Marni von Wilpert -- three Democratic House candidates whose elections will determine control of Congress.
---

Folks, if you are angry about what is happening in this country, then we all have a role to play in doing something about it. And there is probably nothing more important we can do than everything we can to take back the House.

And heaven help us if we lose in November and there is no check on Trump -- we may very well have had our last free and fair election in this country.
---

So while I don't plan on sending a million fundraising emails going forward, this one was important enough to ask, especially before tomorrow's deadline.

[**If taking back the House is important to you, please split a $3 contribution between Democrats Richard Pan, Randy Villegas, and Marni von Wilpert's campaigns for Congress in California. body:
https://hanksforcolorado.com?utm_source=Hanks+for+Colorado&utm_campaign=10fae87dc4-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_06_29_11_27&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-10fae87dc4-586962644

RON HANKS · CONSERVATIVE REPUBLICAN · US HOUSE – DISTRICT 3 · JUNE 30 PRIMARY

** Honoring Fallen Firefighters
------------------------------------------------------------

Let’s Roll.

We mourn the loss of the firefighters on the Utah-Colorado border. Let’s honor their commitment and sacrifice to our beautiful nation with more than prayers and condolences. Those are honorable actions for American citizens, but it is not enough from our government officials.

It’s time for an earnest conversation about the future of the American West—one that includes President Trump. If I win tomorrow’s primary, I will reach out to the White House and urge him to join us here in the district for that discussion. When it is over, we should have proactive courses-of-action that save lives, land and property.

We face massive fuel loads ready to ignite throughout the Western States. Colorado has nearly one billion standing dead trees amid our 24 million forested acres. We know the methods of forest management: thinning, harvesting, controlled burns, and hands-off monitoring. Yet we fall further behind each year as summer heat, winds, and drought hit our dry state and low reservoirs.

I believe it is time to look at different approaches, and to change up what we are doing. Let’s be more proactive, less reactive. Let’s not wait for it to catch fire and then throw brave men and women at it. We must not accept endless out-of-control fires as inevitable.

We lose precious lives every year. We lose homes, livestock, pets, and uncounted numbers of wildlife—including endangered species—every season.

My brother lost his house in a massive wildfire a few years ago. I helped him clean up and rebuild. As we were doing it, we had to dispose of deer carcasses, and incinerated rabbits, squirrels and birds. They burned up trying to flee. These big fires are killing animals by the millions, indiscriminately, without mercy. Some of those animals are endangered. Harvesting and thinning may take some of their habitat, but these thousand-acre fires take all of it. We must make that point to those who advocate limited human-intervention.

As with our water issues, we need to start now on our fire-mitigation priorities. We need renewed Forest Management and Water Availability programs that rival President Kennedy’s vision of the Apollo lunar-landings. Active forest and watershed management are legitimate roles of government. We have the right to demand better—or replace those who won’t prioritize it.

In honor of all the firefighters and personnel we’ve lost over the decades protecting these United States, let’s roll.

I want to help fix these issues. My first bill in the Colorado State Assembly was for the placement of water storage tanks in areas of high fire danger. It will be my priority in the US House as well.

I ask for your vote tomorrow, and then ask that you work with me to implement real, proactive solutions.

Respectfully,

Ron Hanks

body:
We need to put partisan politics aside to help the people of Ohio.

|
---

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134280934/630703096/-1685711049?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOQ15Acton_260629_T1_3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZjE3NTE3NC0xMjc0LWYxMTEtYWM5Yy0wMDBkM2E1NGJlZDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=4qnAcwuBfb7wlGeVadY0ZOU0ElsZ8h767oN3xwTX1T8=) Derek, I’m Dr. Amy Acton, and I’m the Democratic nominee for governor of Ohio.

I grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, struggling through abuse, neglect, and hunger — and even spent one winter living in a tent.

I often share that public schools saved my life. After pulling myself out of poverty, I worked three jobs to put myself through med school.

Throughout my career, I’ve always worked with both sides of the aisle — because I’ll work with anyone who wants to solve problems instead of making them. In 2019, I was appointed by a Republican governor to lead the Ohio Department of Health. I held drug companies accountable, kept communities healthy, and was called to serve during the most unprecedented public health crisis of our lifetimes.

I’m a doctor, not a politician, but I am a public servant.

**I’m running for governor because people in my state are struggling, and I refuse to look the other way while bad actors and special interests keep taking Ohio backwards on nearly every measure.**

The problems we face don’t care if you’re a Democrat or a Republican. They’re just problems that need to be fixed. And Derek, I don’t care if you’re a Democrat or a Republican, either. I’ll fight for you and your family just the same.

_But I can’t win this race alone; that’s why I’m asking for your help today._

| | | | | | Team Mackenzie,Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District here in the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos has one of the largest Latino populations of any district in the Northeastern United States. It’s a community that is central to our local culture and economy, and we have worked hard to ensure that everyone receives the attention and representation that they deserve. That includes hiring Spanish-speaking staff, opening an office in downtown Allentown, and regularly communicating with constituents in Spanish. I have also worked to maintain an open dialogue with Latino community leaders through initiatives such as my _Lunch with a Legislator_ series, which provides an opportunity to hear directly from residents about the issues that matter most to them. Conversations like these helps to ensure the voices of all residents, including the Latino community, are represented in Washington, D.C.In Congress, I remain focused on delivering results for everyone, strengthening economic opportunities, and addressing the needs of all constituents throughout the Greater Lehigh Valley.I am proud to continue fighting for us in Washington and grateful for the support and partnership of so many dedicated Latino leaders across our region.

|

[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0EtqwzAUheHVyLMY6cqW7IEGJcWBQkJLA4FOjB43sahsC0mpt1_cJXT-cQ78t_N41j745XHRM6pU7qNb3Zhj8MWh9dmviy5lwvyMCWccgYI4UHGAflzCyCqnnHWa2QoVkx1IKZmg1aR4I3quGZi2RWg7qjvHmtYYS4HLXtLKq32KCuiBt8C7unFoZQtcuDvvG9CkoTpgKnXC-DTBW70Unb_va7JY23WugppKiZnwFwIDgWHbttrgUiImO-2CwAAngNvX8XokMNw-4eN0edsxH_LTMMJfr-_HKikXNx-Cz0KShj5m7cPfQflHjx8FvwEAAP__pfJsNg)

Republican Task Force Issue: 6/29/2026
Court Buries The Deep State
The Supreme Court handed President Trump a [landmark separation-of-powers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGOozAURb8GOiP7AQYKF9vQZdstkWM_J08x2LIfYT9_lNF8wfRXV-ecf7ftZinS8fhrdzSFw-aT32qOxB4dVUqHZX5iPXPBHTeQoIXUApbtiJtqvfHOW-VaNGqaYZompWX7NEEH5_p5HEbpZy1HqVSQi7bKYY_Kzi2Zz5XUsEA_Qj93g0c3jdBrH_plANsM0kYs3BXM5z2Sswfb-gqpOOxc2ttonsy5Nv2fBtYG1uu6upD-389KB9b62TSw5hSJydUG1h8H4dJZWJQzYhVczj1XYZlxzywCFRQBvXikN5YjFRGpWuFSerXF-HxRjFT11AzysVuK3yD8i25vA18BAAD__1eDgLY) victory Monday, ruling 6-3 that he may fire members of independent federal agencies at will. The decision [buries Humphrey's Executor](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2OozAUhZ_GdEbm8uNQuNiGLttuiW58b8CKMZZtwubtR4zmCaY51dH5-f7d5zs678LyFzc2qTxn2mnO0btCbF12e8BSVs5HTLzxDAoGqQYJ4xz83FRkyBI2tmLT6BtorZtBVasZGWwLZB9K3bgn1qR7hsZiR4hIXDlzRakBRmh7aG91R2x1D-1Az3bsAEWn0HMqdeJ4PLyzGArm13NPlmu7b5U3aykxi_aPgEnAdJ5nTej8J7sloL88AqarRcCkLoFRwPTzRNr9SEXmktyLs3z4_ZTEHGUuWFgmfnPKLixyVPLDmGRMbJk4FOmCXI8trok_WfJ_tkfZk4CpSobi6bx3edCiU8uG7ntGVX5B9m3gKwAA__-xi4tD), the 1935 precedent that shielded the so-called fourth branch from presidential control for ninety years. Writing for the conservative majority, Chief Justice Roberts said officials who wield executive power must answer to the president. The ruling [expands Trump's authority](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1yhCAUhZ8GOxwFhLWgSGO3aVM6LFz0ThAYwLiPn9lMqpSpz5nz833c17vBgHF7Nwfo0vzqkltrDtgcWKyYomlth3rmAgesbGCSDpKyeY1hHTunnXVmtB3oUd2YUmqUQ7drqzx_SCEd-Idwwgo5-dFwMQk3c5hkh_oVNUg2Mz4xfuuFA6smxqXzfBbMEDGYAKX1BfL5CGhNbKZ--lQs9DYdXdB7a7kS_kbYQthyXVd_mbpj3FqK8DQHRigvK2FLhKsStvzeoDadpRG2CKGUkLe_CoVnNtFV2sp5ZJrTBYV6LECT92jRhEoxOsgQHcRGzQbRIrwauqJdvjAErFIRMWyHwfCzt_0D75dm3wEAAP__z3WN5g) over roughly two dozen multimember commissions. Justices spared the Fed in a companion case, but the message was unmistakable: the unaccountable administrative state just lost its constitutional shield. ★★★
Court Greenlights Late Ballots
In a 5-4 ruling that disappointed conservatives, the Supreme Court [upheld Mississippi's law](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFytSAQhZ8GOxxcuXgtKP7G7v5tSmeFVZkgOIAhj58xkypl2v12vjnnvL3mFzrvwvYfD9KprLONds6nd8WScdnFgKXslK8z0UEzCFBcKA7jHPzcNVZbY7EzDelueMIwDJ0Sza7FaNWipF0XXEkucrFkJKxkVmVGlEvj9K0SCkboH9A_W2nJDA_olV37UQIyKdBTKm2i81q8MxgK5vc1JkOtiUfj9V7KmVn_j8HEYKq1thXz7sJWYqBPPFygdL8ymALVzGD6qcFNvFJhMMnH2As1_Cb8OvfobeYe630JxYWNeyzED3SeL-h9LLewSdqe1XnvshqYFNvNv-OVP6z5oeErAAD__7nQiGI) allowing mail ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to five days later. Justices Barrett and Roberts joined the three liberals. President Trump called it a [tremendous loss](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFurDAQRb_GdF6ZMWuWwsVr6Pa1r0SDPSzWGzCyh0T5-4gkX5D66Fzde_89pycmTvvrL27kiyxTzHGqByeJFFJNeUeRlep5FNpoAgNOG6dhmHae2ib6GCK2oSHf9g_o-751plk94NxHa5zp3AzOLc655dEGGCxhO7jYJH9FGQcD2DvYx62LFPo7WBcXO3SAqjPIVORW6DhnTgF3wfp_ySXQLeStYb-KHFXZPwpGBaOstCbmiykYC71ORkl5VzCGfBbRM4owVQXjfehsC4P-WaW_-YaJ9YzMWaompnDZOuKHLntQMDbFx-M9MafqetWZ1yV8VZFfPPfm4TMAAP__01V-kg) and warned that votes counted long after an election invite fraud. Republicans aren't backing down. The RNC and the president argued the decision makes it [more imperative](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGunDAQRb_GdF7BwBpcuEhD99KmRLP2wI5ibGTPLsnfR6zyBa8bje690jm_vpYv5Mhp-4k7uSLrEnJY6hFZAnmunBOKPKm-jkI7LdCC0a3RYJcUl64JLviAnW_IdeME4zh2pm2errND6PvH3aLvyA9jawbfj6tFQ-s62alhd021Biz0d-in2xDIj3foTVh7OwCqocVIRW6FjtcjssckWH-vuXi6-bw30T1Fjqr6HwpmBfN5nrcT65PTJjnRH9w5UbmiCuZEZ1Uwe9wP5C197py2QvWDGBXMg4HJGqtg3vKhQ349IlUd8pl0xTdp3KmwR41e9H8d2udXEb0jR81JPzDGLPX6JqGgcRUqmiJ54Zx0wL8K5qa4cJwcI1czqqHdrvYHSL7h_-3gXwAAAP__kReZaQ) than ever to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship, voter ID, and an Election Day deadline nationwide. ★★★
U.S., Iran Stand Down
Washington and Tehran agreed to [stand down](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFuwyAURb8Gb1jwcLA9MHTxlq4drRd4jmkwpoDjql9fpZ_Q8epK50jn4zpf0Qcf7--4kcl1md3u5pKCr46sL36PWOtK5UiZNppBgOZCcxjnGGbZOOOsQ2kbMrIfoO97qUWzGk3dMA4XAqtgICXFzS3aCZKLdDehdOPNCyU0jKAuoIa2c2T7CyjtFjV2gKwTGCjXNlM6bsFbjBXLY9mzpdbuWxPMWmsqTL0xmBhM53m2y_4d6Syvn8EU_JP4azOYjsJ9xsgToSVeMTwKX_e8HT_8Cytm_nlE4jA22bh0-hB80T3rxH1DH_589R95ngZ-AwAA__-V7nX_) Monday after a weekend of missile exchanges around the Strait of Hormuz tested their fragile interim deal, with a U.S. official confirming vessels can again move freely. President Trump announced Iran had [requested a meeting](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDHOnDAQRk8DnVcwBpstXKSh-9OmRIM9LKO1DfF4Q5TTR-QIqb-np0_vx9fyhRw5v75jIlfqtoQjLHJGroE8Cx8Za91JPmehRAt0YFRnFDyXHJe-DS74gL1vyfV2Amttb7p2d2Hswzpua9jMBPrZbeuw6WAtwNQP2owtu1vVGXiCHkFPjyGQtyNoEzb9HACbocNIpT4KnZ81ssdcUd7bUTw9_JHa6PZaT2n0twbmBubruh4Xys75VY9MvzFxpnKjDcyZLrmZo8TQwDwYmPQIDcy1fNKpuGBWhX5-SCoFlYgq55c66Q_J_mbMykfkJGrlGPnIolCEqqhCkVDodrbFhfO6dzG2GbpXQo7_ntb_CPvLwd8AAAD__9drixk) in Doha on Tuesday, though Tehran disputed any talks were scheduled. 0Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Qatar. U.N. Ambassador Mike Waltz said [Iran is isolated](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1uwyAURp8Gb1hw_YMZGLp4S9eO1g1cJzQYW4BDH79yH6Hjp086Rzpft-WGPvj4-MSNTCrr4na35CP44sj67PeIpTwpn0eijRYQMHIxctBLDItsnHHWobQNGakmUErJUTRP06thIqdIdgOCFU7r-ySlnfq7BkkaGm8ulBhBQzdAN7W9I6sG6Ea3droHZL3AQKm0iY7zHrzFWDC_1j1Zau2-NcE8Szky6z4YzAzmWmu77j-Rar5-BnPwb-LXZjCfmfuEkZd0brxi4gehJV4wvDL_PiNxmJpk3FF9CD6PivXisaEPf67yjzRvA78BAAD__1skc_4) as never before. The upside for Americans: oil fell near $70 a barrel, and gas slipped under $3.90 — relief Trump credits to the ceasefire framework.
Letlow Caps Trump's Revenge on Cassidy

Rep. Julia Letlow [cruised to victory](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFurDAQAL8GOiNjOAyFi9fQ3WtToj17faxibMtejuTvo8snpB5pNJqP-3YHChSf_-FAU9hvLrmt5kDs0FKlFIF5x3rmggduSqpJyEmoZYth61tnnHXQ2xZNr2elte4n2e5GD84__AMAFhgt-pvVEv20zMMo536ULZm3Sk5qUcNNDXM3OrT6pobJ-WEZFTSjhICFu4L5fASyEBnqp0_FYmfT0QazM-faDP8atTZqva6r8-kr4lXfvFFrToGYbG3UyuU8sqg2FawCYuIdi8DoUql4YGRxURQhnVQJIoiKERhFOWPyXrzIcirfbTEuXxQC1Uk3o3weQOE3hf9w7mXUTwAAAP__VRaCkQ) in Louisiana's GOP Senate runoff Saturday, beating John Fleming 57-43. Her win completes Trump's revenge against Bill Cassidy and all but locks up the deep-red seat for November.

★★★
Socialists Storm New York

Mamdani-backed socialists [swept New York's primaries](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDHOnDAQRk9jOlZmYO2fwkUauk2bEg32AKMYgzyzIbl9tDlCuq_49PT0frzmF3Lmsn3Hg0LVdU5nmuXKrIkiC58FVXeS91XpoBksuNa6Fsa55LlrUkgxYRcbCp3_Au9952yzh_XpXFwX6gGijbgu0EfrOzfatA5-oYbDB2UdjNA_of96DImif0Lv0tqPA6AZLGaq-qh0vZfMEYui_FzPGukRz6PJYVe9xPTfDEwGpvu-HzfKzmXTs9BvPLhQ_VwNTIVuMTBFPC7krXz24MB5_zQwyRkZM4tKK-8YSaTFotySKC6ZZT-oaCtaUWn7Y2BqakjXzTmzOG8Gux3I-Z-U_kfDXwH-BgAA__9a3oPz), ousting two incumbents and rattling Democratic leaders. The DSA is now eyeing seats from Denver to D.C., turning Schumer and Jeffries' own backyard into a launchpad for the hard left.

★★★
Schumer's Primary Peril Grows

The fallout is reaching the top: one analyst predicts Schumer [won't survive a primary](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2ynDAQhE8jMm3BIMQSKHBC9pw6pAZpgLH1Q0lisW_v2j3Cyzro6urv-_W1fCF7jvtPDGRy3RaX3FJOz9WR5cIpYq0HlevMFGiBFrRstYRpiX7pGmecddjZhkw3PmEcx063zWGe27DCMFjslOtAW0eqAzVN2zrgtq6qYfOeajVM0A_QPx_KkR0H6LXb-kkBCtWip1wfmc5r9WwxVix_tpQtPWwKjTdHrWcR_Q8Bs4D5vu_HjeXguNcU6S8GjpTfVQFzpLsImC2GE3mPn5zinql8EL2AWWkYez0JmIs9rkBZ3ilWWa784hdJlGfmgPmfxB05lipRuoLSYnTssJL8nUjaFO2BAuYmG3fe7D0XPQrV7gHZf37Xb2h-GfgfAAD__x-xkB8) against a DSA challenger, floating AOC as the likeliest 2028 threat. Democratic infighting is only intensifying.

* * *
SAVE Act Freezes House

House conservatives have frozen the floor, demanding the Senate pass the SAVE America Act, while Trump presses Leader Thune to nuke the filibuster. South Dakota's GOP even [moved to censure](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGupSAURb8GO4weEbWgmMbuTjulORcOwlwEAzjO57_4PuG1O3vvrKw_r-2FPvi4_8aDVK52M8ls5Qy-GtK--BSxVkflOjMdtEEHkneSw7LFsPWNUUYb7HVDqp9mmKapl13j1DiPb7LaSCOEJUsA8q0XuxgBZrAzNl49V52EBYYRhrkVhvQ0wiCNHRYByESHgXJtM53XO3iNsWL52JQ1tTodTVCu1rOw4ReDlcF633d7Y3E-7jVF-o-Hj5SfKoM10l0YrIUiVmKwCglTP4onSld13OAnVeR7OrmmWK5MPFn-N7nIq7viM2myMuftQ_BFTkx0-4E-fJPUH4j7p-ArAAD__8qVf1A) Thune before voting it down.★★★
Trump Gains Firing Power

The Slaughter ruling grants Trump sweeping authority to fire independent agency heads. The White House [welcomed the decision](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0D3O4yAUheHV4M6WfU0gFBTTuMu0U1oEruOr4U-AQ5Y_yizh6x8dHb1_HvvDkKf4-m0C6tKO3SW31-ypObRUKUXT2on1ygUD7jCDGGcxgtqj35fBaWedWeyAepF3kFIuYh5O_eRcCnOAUng4RLEcdlaLlWpBOMRqBtLfqVmAgvUG633iDq28wSrcsSoOhvHZeCxtKpivpydrYjP175GKxcmmMHh9tpYrW38x2Bhsvfepm3pSfLUU8WMCRSxfymCL2OvXnNRwPNNVkcHGBdxvijPYWrlCHjt6mwLWET_ZRIduxA_aq9Ebx5w6FgbbULTLnbynKiTj8ysY8v__tB_ke2v4FwAA__-N4IGx), with the president vowing to install loyal appointees across commissions Congress once kept beyond his reach.

★★★
FISA Powers Remain Lapsed
